notes: All five documents share the reference PIS/2026/091 and/or PO-1009, so they are grouped as one transaction. Two notable inconsistencies reduce confidence: (1) INV-1009-A and INV-1009-B are explicitly labeled as first and second scans of the same invoice with identical amounts, dates, and references, indicating duplicate submission rather than two distinct transactions - only one should be treated as the operative invoice, though both are retained here for completeness; (2) the purchase order amount (INR 118,000.00, tax INR 18,000.00) does not match the invoiced and paid amount (INR 141,600.00, tax INR 21,600.00), a discrepancy of INR 23,600.00 that is unexplained by any document in the set - no PO amendment, change order, or approval document is present to justify the higher invoiced/paid amount. The bank statement and ledger entry are internally consistent with the invoice total and with each other, and the payment date (2026-07-22) logically follows the invoice date (2026-07-15) which follows the PO date (2026-07-03), but this internal consistency does not resolve the PO-to-invoice amount mismatch nor confirm that goods were actually received. No goods receipt or delivery confirmation document is present in this transaction to verify that the goods/services corresponding to PO-1009 and invoice PIS/2026/091 were received prior to payment; this is treated as missing evidence rather than assumed absent-by-policy, since no pattern across other transactions in this case exists to support a goods-receipt exemption for this vendor. The successful NEFT payment shown in BNK-1009 does not by itself establish that any receipt-based payment term was satisfied.
